races.name: Trustmark Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Level Up
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist with consistent 5f Good-ground form (three top-three finishes in last four on similar going), making this trip and surface ideal; Alexandra McDonnell's 7lb claim helps offset the 140lb burden, and two days' freshness is no concern for a horse who handled similar quick turnarounds.

runners_data.name: Sonic Si
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's four-year-old arrives in red-hot form with back-to-back wins, both over 5f including one on Good ground, and the 5lb claim for Matthew Lloyd Slater is a tangible asset; the sim-going record (1 win from 1 on Good) underlines the surface suitability and this horse looks the most likely to control the race shape.

runners_data.name: Vape
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran whose recent form string shows a sharp drop in trip from 6-7f to 5f and whose last ten runs have largely been in rear-of-field roles — a true hold-up horse that the map has redistributed to midfield; the 1-from-1 recent 6f Good win is appealing but the condensed trip and likely inability to get a true back-marker position temper the outlook, and STYLE_FIT of 0.92 should be respected.

runners_data.name: So Smart
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's seven-year-old carries tongue-tie and has not won at 5f Good for some time (1W3P sim-going from 15 runs), though the horse has placed consistently; racing naturally from the rear but here shuffled forward in the map, it will not find its ideal rhythm unless the race truly collapses into a crawl.

runners_data.name: Hallandale Beach
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with unknown style whose last three runs over 5f on Good produced a best of third place; Kevin Philippart De Foy's runner has no Going concern but the consistent placing without a win and an unknown pace preference make this the pivotal unknown quantity — if Taryn Langley pushes forward they could set the race up for a rival, if they sit the race shape shifts entirely.

runners_data.name: Bridget's Baby
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's lightly-raced three-year-old carries the lightest weight in the field at 121lbs but is a natural hold-up horse crammed into a midfield slot on the map due to the volume of rear-runners; best recent run was second over 5f on Good but the form is thin (06-72 recent string) and the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90 reflects the uncomfortable positional compromise.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field, Ffos Las' 5f on Good ground is set to produce a cautious, tactical opener where nobody is clearly committed to making the running from the gate. Hallandale Beach (style unknown) is the wild card who could push forward and set a moderate tempo, but if they sit, the field drifts into a bunched sprint with a wall of horses hitting the line together from around the 2f pole. That scenario — a compressed, end-to-end dash — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types who can travel smoothly and produce a single surge late, rather than pure hold-up horses who need a true pace scenario to peel off the back. This field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate: Vape, So Smart, and Bridget's Baby are genuine rear-of-field horses pushed forward visually on the map, with Level Up and Sonic Si the most likely to naturally secure the prominent ground they need when racing gets underway.

watchPoints.text: Sonic Si has won two of his last two and holds the only confirmed winning recent strike on Good ground over 5f — watch whether Matthew Lloyd Slater pushes for position early, as that move will define the entire race shape.

Hallandale Beach's unknown running style is the key tactical uncertainty; if Taryn Langley goes forward from the gate this horse sets the pace and potentially becomes a pacemaker for others, so monitor the first furlong closely.

Vape, So Smart, and Bridget's Baby are all natural hold-up horses mapped forward due to overcrowding at the rear — if all three jostle for midfield space in the opening furlong, the early stages could be ragged and disruptive to other runners.

Level Up has run twice in the last two days, suggesting connections are happy with the horse's condition, but Alexandra McDonnell's 7lb claim is a notable advantage in a field where weight differentials range from 121lbs to 143lbs.

Ffos Las 5f on Good is a flat, undemanding track — there is no stamina gradient to stretch the field, meaning early position is especially important and horses that miss the break are unlikely to recover ground in a compressed sprint finish.

races.name: Carmarthenshire Hunt Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands C and D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cavan Lady
runners_data.note: Lightly raced two-year-old for Richard Hughes with Finley Marsh in the saddle; sole run was a third on soft over five furlongs suggesting she handles cut ground, and stepping onto good here is an unknown — style is unclassified so early market moves will be informative.

runners_data.name: Nasserein
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's two-year-old raced only once, finishing fifth over six furlongs on firm for Pierre-Louis Jamin; dropping to five furlongs on good ground could suit if she has natural speed, but the single run leaves her profile genuinely open.

runners_data.name: Tango Hotel
runners_data.note: Hold-up type by style for George Scott, with headgear noted and a run on good ground in the book — finished fifth in that outing; Liam Wright claims five pounds, and the horse's best form on a similar surface (sim-going: 1 placed) offers a small reference point, though no wins and no placed finishes on turf cap expectation.

runners_data.name: Defiant Dream
runners_data.note: Mark Usher runner whose sole form figure is a ninth over six furlongs on standard Tapeta; a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping here because the rear is crowded — Tyler Heard partners a horse stepping to turf for the first time, and the fading-in-finish flag combined with racing out of natural role tempers any optimism.

runners_data.name: Leading Raya
runners_data.note: Also trained by Mark Usher and carrying the same fades-in-finish flag; a last-place effort over six furlongs on soft is the only form guide, and Rose Dawes claims five pounds — the going change to good and drop to five furlongs would need to unlock significant improvement for this filly to feature.

runners_data.name: Past Passion
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's filly has two runs over this exact five-furlong trip at Good, placing second on her better effort; confirmed front-runner whose style fits naturally at the head of affairs, though the STYLE_FIT tag at 0.90 acknowledges she is pushed slightly out of optimal role in the overall race shape — 40 days off is the only mild query, but Callum Hutchinson is an experienced pairing for this spot.

races.paceDynamic: Past Passion is the lone confirmed front-runner in this six-runner maiden, and with no genuine pace rival to push her, she should be able to dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable gallop on good ground over five furlongs at Ffos Las. Defiant Dream and Leading Raya are natural hold-up types pushed toward midfield on the map due to the imbalance of rear-position horses, but neither is a natural front-runner capable of disrupting Past Passion's rhythm. Cavan Lady and Nasserein arrive as unknown quantities stylistically, meaning the early pace picture could clarify quickly once stalls open, but the default shape is a controlled lead from Past Passion into a straightforward sprint finish. This race shape strongly favours horses with the tactical speed to sit just off the pace and pounce when the leader's advantage is modest — prominent-to-midfield runners who can respond to a steady early gallop will be better placed than true hold-up types waiting for a pace that may never truly collapse. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Past Passion is most likely to secure the front position, with Tango Hotel and Defiant Dream unable to get the back-marker berths their natural styles prefer.

scenarios.body: If Past Passion goes unchallenged to the front and sets a measured, controlled gallop that suits her rhythm.

scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and true closers find sufficient run room to charge through.

scenarios.title: Pace Injection Breaks Rhythm
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unknown-style runners — Cavan Lady or Nasserein — challenges for the lead early and forces a contested gallop.
scenarios.body: If one of the unknown-style runners — Cavan Lady or Nasserein — challenges for the lead early and forces a contested gallop.

scenarios.trigger: If Past Passion over-reaches her early advantage and weakens inside the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Past Passion's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single biggest race-shape determinant — watch whether Cavan Lady or Nasserein's handlers instruct an early push to test her, which would fundamentally alter the pace picture.

Defiant Dream and Leading Raya are both tagged as fading-in-finish types and are racing out of their natural rear positions; if they are asked to settle in midfield rather than hunt the pace, their chances of finishing races that have frustrated them before look slim.

Both Mark Usher runners (Defiant Dream and Leading Raya) share the same trainer who has a 1/7 record over the last 14 days — monitor any signs of stable confidence in either runner through market moves before post time.

Tango Hotel's headgear and a sim-going placed run are worth tracking in-running — if Past Passion's gallop is genuinely uncontested and modest, a horse with a small form reference on good ground sitting second or third could find the final furlong easier than its overall record implies.

Lightly raced fillies (Cavan Lady and Nasserein) with unclassified styles could break sharply and inject unexpected pace — watch the first furlong closely to see whether either goes with Past Passion before the race settles into its expected shape.

races.name: Blackmore Building Contractors Handicap

runners_data.name: Senor Campanaro
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard and has placed form at the trip, but similar-going record (0W0P in 3 runs) is a flag; Ashley Lewis claims 5lb which helps the handicapper, but this horse needs things to fall right from the back.|

runners_data.name: Katie's Song
runners_data.note: Limited form — only three runs, all on Standard ground, and now faces Good turf for the first time with no win to her name; Finley Marsh rides for Richard Hughes whose 14-day strike rate of 5/24 is solid, but the evidence base here is thin.|

runners_data.name: Who Is Alice
runners_data.note: Steps up sharply to 7½f having run exclusively over 5-6f, which is the key question; two placed efforts on Soft suggest she handles cut, and her Good-ground record (6 runs, 1W2P) is reasonable, though the trip extension is a significant unknown for Grace Harris's filly.|

runners_data.name: Kingofthecarnival
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard and ran creditably at the trip before; his true racing style is a genuine hold-up runner consigned to the midfield band because the field is saturated with closers — he'll need fortune in running at 7½f on Good, and the headgear note (previously wore a hood) is worth monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Red Moon
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground over 7f just three days ago for Jack Channon, making this a quick bounce-back and a stamina step to 7½f; the freshness concern is real, but his Good-going record (1W1P from 3 runs) and natural hold-up style that may push forward given the lack of pace make him one of the more interesting runners — though he is at heart a hold-up type forced into a prominent role by the race shape.|

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Three runs all on Standard, all mid-division finishes (4th, 6th, 4th), with no win to her name and now first run in 51 days; Andrew Balding is a quality handler and the T14 rate of 6/36 is decent, but Thai Princess's form profile offers little encouragement, and having a hood (hg:t) on a filly returning from 51 days off adds a layer of uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Gelato
runners_data.note: Modest form — best finish is 6th, all runs on Good or Soft, and the step up from sprint distances to 7½f is untested; Adrian Wintle's 14-day record of 0/9 gives no confidence from the training perspective, and her Good-ground profile (0W0P from 5 runs) is uninspiring.|

runners_data.name: Phantom Shadow
runners_data.note: Placed twice on Firm over 8f at what looks a stiffer test, and now drops to handicap company at 7½f on Good; Harry Charlton sends out a horse with headgear (hg:t) who has shown he stays the trip well — the switch from Firm to Good is a going question, but his stamina profile is the most compelling in the field for a stay-on finish.|

runners_data.name: Distillation
runners_data.note: Lowest rated runner in the field at OR=52, with recent form of 2nd over 7f on Standard as the sole encouragement; Mark Usher's 14-day strike rate of 1/5 is limited sample size, and this filly faces a step up in class without the ratings or form to suggest she can bridge the gap from the rear.|

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field at 7½f on Good ground at Ffos Las, the race is likely to begin at a crawl before accelerating sharply in the straight, favouring those who can quicken from behind. Every single runner in this field carries a hold-up profile, meaning there is no natural pace-setter to string the field out — the early gallop will almost certainly be modest, compressing the field and turning this into a dash from well inside the final two furlongs. The absence of any genuine leader means the race will be run to suit closers in theory, but in practice the sprint finish becomes a lottery determined by position and luck in running. Red Moon (recent winner on Good, quick turnaround), Phantom Shadow (placed form on Firm, step to 7½f interesting), and Kingofthecarnival (won at the trip) are the most likely to force their way forward from the hold-up pack and secure the best position entering the home straight — this race shape unambiguously favours horses who can travel smoothly in the pack and produce a sharp, powerful finish over the final two furlongs rather than those who need a true pace to aim at.

watchPoints.text: Red Moon ran just three days ago and while his Good-ground win is a strong qualifier, watch whether he travels fluently early — a horse returning this quickly could either be super-sharp or show signs of fatigue in the closing stages at 7½f.

Phantom Shadow wears a hood and steps from Firm to Good for the first time — watch his behaviour at the start and whether the headgear change produces the desired focus, as his 8f placed form on Firm is the most interesting stamina credential in the race.

With all nine runners holding genuine hold-up profiles, watch for a dangerously slow early gallop — if no horse shows any inclination to go forward in the first two furlongs, the race risks becoming a lottery decided purely by draw position and luck in running.

Kingofthecarnival is the one runner here with a recent win at exactly this trip and distance combination on a comparable surface — watch whether Harry Vigors (claiming 7lb) pushes forward aggressively from the outset given there is nothing else to set the pace.

Who Is Alice has never raced beyond 6f — watch her early to see whether she settles and travels within herself, as any sign of pulling or racing keenly over the first two furlongs would undermine her stamina claims on this step up to 7½f.

races.name: RHN Travel Handicap

runners_data.name: Marlborough Place
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 8f on Good and placed over 7f on the same surface — solid sim-going record of 1W2P; 112 days off is the main query but Adrian Wintle sends runners back fit and Taryn Langley's 5lb claim is a useful weight advantage here.

runners_data.name: Huscal
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type for Charles Hills but has a patchy recent record at 7f on Good, finishing 8th and 12th in his last two attempts at the trip/going combination; tongue-tie and pad headgear suggest connections are trying to sharpen him up, and Thomas Greatrex takes the mount after a yard in form (3/13 T14).

runners_data.name: Great Dream
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner who is genuinely a prominent-going horse but finds himself pushed into a midfield slot here because the prominent berths are filled — his best form (3rd, 1st at 7f on Tapeta/Soft) may not fully translate; the pace headgear is noted and LR of just 5 days suggests connections are busy with him.

runners_data.name: Factual
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter with a STYLE_FIT flag indicating slight positional uncertainty; two wins at 6-7f on Good and Tapeta underpin his credentials as a front-runner, and Callum Hutchinson for Andrew Balding (7/49 T14) is a big-yard angle worth noting over this trip where a solo lead is likely.

runners_data.name: Sunny Smile
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Hugo Palmer who won over 6f on Good and has placed at 6f, making the step to 7½f a live question; tongue-tie retained from last run and a 12-day turnaround suggests freshness is not a concern, though she'll need the pace to lift to close from the rear of the field.

runners_data.name: Dagger Strike
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a string of placed efforts (four consecutive seconds at 7f) who needs a strong gallop to close; the blinkers are a new addition for Archie Watson and Harry Vigors claims 7lb, but sim-going record of 0 wins from 9 tries is a flag — he gets close but hasn't converted.

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner whose last three runs show a win, a second, and a 6th at 7f, but the race map has him occupying a midfield position he won't naturally settle into; blinkers on for Harry Charlton and a 21-day freshener, but the positional compromise at OR=75 makes this tough.

races.paceDynamic: Factual is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 7½f trip on Good ground at Ffos Las. Marlborough Place and Huscal will press from prominent positions just behind, creating a compact early order rather than a war of attrition, meaning fractions are unlikely to be punishing. This field carries more prominent-running intent than the race shape can accommodate — Great Dream and Slight Of Foot are natural front-runners who will be shuffled back into midfield roles they do not naturally suit, compromising their effectiveness. The resulting race shape — one controlled pace-setter, two honest stalkers, and hold-up horses Sunny Smile and Dagger Strike needing the tempo to lift — favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs rather than those relying on a strong late gallop to close ground.

watchPoints.text: Marlborough Place returning after 112 days — watch how sharply he moves to the front early; if he travels prominently and comfortably past the 3f pole he is a serious threat to take the race over.

Great Dream and Slight Of Foot — both natural front-runners squeezed into midfield; watch for either racing keenly or pulling wide in the first 2f, which could disrupt Factual's lead and change the shape of the race entirely.

Dagger Strike has placed four times consecutively without winning at 7f on Soft/Standard — watch whether the new blinkers trigger a more positive response or whether he simply runs into another place at best.

Factual's gallop pace in the first 3f will be the key race-shape indicator — if he's allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable clip, the race is likely to be won from the front three; if Huscal or Marlborough Place pushes him, watch for the hold-up horses to close late.

races.name: Blackmore Building Contractors Handicap

runners_data.name: Pay Attention
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer with moderate Good-ground form (9 wins and places from 15 similar-going runs) who arrives 33 days fresh; trainer Faye Bramley has a quiet 14-day record (1/9) and apprentice Oliver Carmichael takes off 7lb, but this horse's tendency to race from the rear will leave it dependent on a strong pace that Fifty Sent is unlikely to generate.|

runners_data.name: Devious Devan
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick's runner returns quickly (13 days) and won last time out at Sandown, but that victory came on Standard artificial ground where pace dynamics differed; a genuine deep hold-up type whose true finishing position sits well behind what the map shows, and the Good Ffos Las surface yields only 4 comparable form references from 15 runs.|

runners_data.name: Rosemary's Rose
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's four-year-old has placed twice from four attempts on similar going and showed consistency across the summer, but she is a true rear-rank horse who will be carried further forward than ideal by the crowded hold-up contingent — her chance hinges on the pace being strong enough to come back to her, which looks questionable.|

runners_data.name: Bobby Dassler
runners_data.note: Won last time out just two days ago, a very quick turnaround that warrants close watching for freshness; races in a tongue-tie and is a natural hold-up type over 8-12 furlongs on Good ground (7 similar-going runs, 1W 3P), but the redistribution dynamic means Mason Paetel (5lb claim) will struggle to position him where Barry John Murphy intends.|

runners_data.name: Fifty Sent
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and therefore the pivotal horse for all pace scenarios; two consecutive wins, both on Standard ground, but the Good turf here is an unexplored variable (only 2 comparable runs, 0W 0P) — if Zoe Lewis (7lb) can replicate that front-running dominance on turf, this horse is structurally very well placed to last home.|

runners_data.name: Quick Turn
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's three-year-old arrives quickly (4 days) and has won twice over this exact trip including on Good ground, with a solid recent record (4 runs on similar going, 1 placed); Harry Vigors (7lb) is a positive claim, and this horse's tactical profile — capable of sitting prominently off a slow pace — suits this race shape better than most rivals.|

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: David Evans is in excellent 14-day form (4/14) and this three-year-old has won on Good ground over a mile at Ffos Las, making the course-and-distance angle compelling; a hold-up horse by nature whose mapped midfield position flatters her typical pitch, but if George Downing can bridge that gap she has the form profile to be competitive.|

runners_data.name: U S S Constitution
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner, so has no bearing on the race outcome; noted for completeness — Ed Walker's six-year-old was a genuine hold-up type with veteran form who would have added to the redistributed cluster.|

races.paceDynamic: Fifty Sent is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate an uncontested, controlled pace from the front over Ffos Las's flat mile on Good ground. With one horse setting a sustainable tempo and the remainder of the field — Pay Attention, Quick Turn, Bobby Dassler, Devious Devan, Rosemary's Rose, Alice's Influence, and the non-runner U S S Constitution — all natural hold-up or midfield types, the early gallop is unlikely to be truly searching, favouring a horse who can travel prominently or close from a handy position rather than one making up ground from the rear. The redistribution note is significant here: Devious Devan, Rosemary's Rose, Bobby Dassler, Alice's Influence, and U S S Constitution are all genuine hold-up horses pushed into the mapped midfield simply because the field is overwhelmingly rear-loaded, meaning they cannot all secure a truly prominent pitch, and few if any will genuinely race near the pace. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a relaxed pace with a wall of closers behind — strongly favours a horse capable of sitting just off the leader in second or third and kicking early, rather than horses forced to close from further back than their trainer intends; Quick Turn, who has the tactical pace and recent winning form over this exact trip and going, is the profile that stands to benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Fifty Sent's Good-turf record is thin (0 wins, 0 places from 2 comparable runs) — if the switch from Standard ground costs her momentum in front, the entire pace shape of the race unravels and every scenario probability shifts.

Quick Turn ran just four days ago; watch the market closely at the off — if Ian Williams has him fresh and ready, the quick turnaround is a positive flag, but if he looks flat in the parade ring, his prominent-sit profile becomes far less reliable.

Bobby Dassler raced only two days ago — an exceptionally tight turnaround for a seven-year-old, and signs of fatigue in the early to middle stages would materially weaken Scenario B, where his hold-up strength is most needed.

With U S S Constitution a non-runner, the field is reduced to seven effective runners, thinning the hold-up pack slightly — watch whether any remaining horse instinctively moves to track Fifty Sent early, which would alter whether Fifty Sent truly runs unchallenged.

Alice's Influence carries the strongest trainer angle (David Evans, 4/14 over 14 days) and has winning course-and-distance form on Good ground — worth monitoring for any market support that might signal the team expects her to overcome the unfavourable pace shape.

races.name: Oil 4 Wales Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Poor Relation
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front runner with a clear path to the lead; Stevie Donohoe will have the ride easy from the front off Good ground, though her last three runs show inconsistency and stepping up from 8f-10f may ask questions of her stamina at this trip.

runners_data.name: Alikalu
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and entirely unknown in terms of style, going preference and trip; Pierre-Louis Jamin takes the ride for Jack Jones whose yard has had two winners from eleven runners in the last fourteen days, making this one to treat with caution as a potential dark horse.

runners_data.name: Blue Tulip
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick's filly has struggled in two starts — fifth and eighth — and her natural inclination is to race from the rear; in this race, however, the hold-up population is large enough that she is unlikely to find open space from her preferred position, compounding an already moderate form profile.

runners_data.name: Evening Fades
runners_data.note: William Haggas's filly showed a solid fourth on her sole start at 8f on Tapeta, and her one run on Good ground was a sixth over a longer trip; she is a genuine hold-up horse and needs a stronger pace than Poor Relation is likely to set for Darragh Keenan to deliver her effectively.

runners_data.name: Lady Magu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian runner whose style is uncertain but who has twice finished fifth at 10f, once on Good — her record at the trip and on the going is 0 wins from 2 tries; Harry Vigors's claim could be a factor in a weak field but her consistency has yet to emerge.

runners_data.name: Miss Malone To You
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's filly has been off 53 days and wears a hood, which adds a layer of uncertainty; a true hold-up operator whose two runs produced a fifth on Good and an eighth on Tapeta, and the absence, headgear change, and poor draw of positions behind a single moderate pacer all work against her.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: OR of just 69 marks her out as the class inferior in this field, but she is one of only two horses with a naturally prominent style; George Downing has a platform to sit second to Poor Relation and could prove a surprise force if the favourite fails to last home, with one place from four runs her best to date.

runners_data.name: Feelin' Free
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Jack Jones — same yard as Alikalu — with no known style, going preference or trip evidence; Finley Marsh takes the ride and the total absence of form data makes any assessment speculative, though fresh runners from small strings can occasionally spring surprises in weak maidens.

races.paceDynamic: Poor Relation is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push her, she is expected to stride into an uncontested lead and set a sustainable, measured tempo over this mile-and-a-quarter trip on Good ground. Ziata is the only other horse with a prominent style, but her OR of 69 and modest form string suggest she is unlikely to apply meaningful pressure to the leader. The remainder of the field — Evening Fades, Blue Tulip, and Miss Malone To You — are genuine hold-up types, while Alikalu and Feelin' Free are unknown quantities who may or may not find prominent ground. This race shape — a lone pace-setter controlling a modest gallop with closers unable to force the issue — classically favours a horse that can sit just behind the leader and quicken off the steady pace, meaning prominent-to-midfield trackers who travel smoothly are best placed; genuine hold-up horses requiring a strong pace to power through are at a disadvantage. Note that while Blue Tulip is a natural hold-up runner, the field's hold-up population is sufficient that she is redistributed to a midfield slot on the map — but her actual racing style remains rear-end, not midfield.

scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely slow and the front runner quickens from a long way out, denying late runners any real gap to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Storm Home

scenarios.body: If the pace quickens sufficiently from the top of the home straight to generate a strong enough tempo for genuine closers to pass beaten rivals.

watchPoints.text: Poor Relation holds all the pace cards — watch whether she is ridden to dominate or is allowed to coast, as the tempo she sets will determine whether any closer can land a blow in the straight.

Blue Tulip is a natural rear-runner who is unlikely to secure her preferred position in a field stacked with hold-up types; watch for traffic problems or a wide run if Jack Dace tries to push her forward against her instincts.

Alikalu and Feelin' Free are both Jack Jones debutants with zero public form — if either is well-backed on course before the off, treat that as live market intelligence in an otherwise data-starved scenario.

Evening Fades represents William Haggas, typically a shrewd handler in fillies' maidens, but her hold-up style is poorly suited to the anticipated steady gallop; watch whether Darragh Keenan tries to improve her position earlier than usual to compensate.

Ziata's lowly OR of 69 is a significant class flag, but her prominent style makes her the only horse capable of sitting directly behind Poor Relation and exploiting a modest pace — watch her market drift or hold as a guide to confidence from the Ed Walker yard.

races.name: Josh Perry BPRFC Supporters Player Of The Year Handicap

runners_data.name: Zooter
runners_data.note: Has placed twice over 10f on Good ground which is directly applicable here, and as a naturally hold-up type for Jack Jones, she may find herself drifting to the lead by default in this runner-less-than-eager field — the key question is whether Finley Marsh pushes forward or stays patient.|

runners_data.name: Liveinthelight
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's yard is in decent recent form (6/22 over 14 days) but this horse has finished ninth and fifth in its last two runs on Good ground, and its true hold-up style — bumped to midfield on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded — means it faces the dual challenge of poor recent form and an unfamiliar tactical position.|

runners_data.name: Tales Old As Time
runners_data.note: A lengthy 237-day absence for this two-year-old makes fitness a real question mark, and form figures of 10-8-3 show a horse yet to put a complete run together; naturally a hold-up type, it could find itself on or near the pace by default, which may not suit its profile at all.|

runners_data.name: Rajwaah
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's charge has form figures of 9-10-6 across its last three, all on going ranging from Good to Standard, and its true hold-up style being pushed into a midfield mapping role underlines the awkward position it will find itself in when nobody else wants to lead — Pierre-Louis Jamin will need to be creative.|

runners_data.name: Grand Pier
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex sends this horse out having placed at 1/15 over the trainer's last 14 days, and Grand Pier has shown ability to finish in the frame over 10f on Good ground; its natural reluctance to be prominent is the same as the rest of this field, so apprentice Harry Vigors faces the same positional puzzle as everyone else.|

runners_data.name: Blue Jammin
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Soft ground and ran back just nine days ago, so fitness is not the concern here — the concern is that its fading-in-finish tendency and its true hold-up style being squeezed into midfield mapping creates a double difficulty, and OR 53 leaves it the least-exposed on paper but also the least proven.|

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners carrying a hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 1m2f contest at Ffos Las faces a genuine tactical vacuum from the outset — nobody wants to lead, and the early gallop is likely to be crawling, creating a bunched, slow-burn race that explodes into a sprint up the straight. Zooter and Tales Old As Time, as the two horses without a redistribution flag, are the most likely to find themselves drifting forward simply by default rather than design, as the field idles and positions compress. The Good ground suits a sharp, resolute finisher rather than a grinding stayer, and the flat Ffos Las track with its long straight rewards horses who can quicken out of a pack in the final two furlongs. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Liveinthelight, Rajwaah, Grand Pier, and Blue Jammin are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning several will be racing outside their natural zone; the horse best able to adapt and quicken from a midfield berth in a sprint finish holds the clearest advantage.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Zooter or Tales Old As Time drifts to the front in the opening furlong — whoever leads by default in this hold-up-only field controls the tempo and the race shape entirely.

Liveinthelight's "fades in finish" flag combined with its redistribution out of true hold-up position means it could be caught in no-man's land — watch for it travelling prominently but weakening where it matters.

Blue Jammin ran just nine days ago; watch its early demeanour and whether it shows any signs of a below-par effort under the burden of a quick turnaround in a race with no pace to drag it into contention.

With all six horses carrying hold-up profiles, watch the two-furlong pole — if the field is still bunched at that point, the widest-drawn or best-positioned runner to find clear daylight will have a decisive advantage regardless of form.
